HSTU’s intervention targets follow its computation: projected U/Q/K/V, SiLU-based attention aggregation with relative position/time bias, normalized aggregation multiplied by gate U, output projection, and residual addition. Unlike softmax attention, aggregation weights are not normalized across sequence positions. These components provide plausible locations for tracing final-item dependence, but attention weights alone do not establish causal contribution. A jointly trained lexical residual is implementation-specific; inspect its actual insertion point separately from the original architecture. [HSTU paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152)

Activation-patching research supports paired clean/corrupted runs, replacing selected internal activations and measuring output recovery; conclusions depend strongly on corruption and metric choices. For this task, a proposed adaptation is to freeze one checkpoint per category, perturb the final observed item using a matched real-item replacement, and reversibly patch gates, aggregation outputs, positional contributions, and lexical residual activations. Measure changes in the same target-minus-negative score margins, using the final nonpadding readout and fixed candidates. Include identity-patch checks, reverse-direction patches, and component ablations; restore hooks and state after every intervention. [Patching best practices](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/06a52a54c8ee03cd86771136bc91eb1f-Abstract-Conference.html)

Gradient-based attribution patching can cheaply screen components, but its linear approximation should be checked against actual intervention-induced margin changes, especially around multiplicative gates. Report signed effects, variation across users/categories, and sensitivity to replacement choice. Treat findings as checkpoint-specific computational sensitivity: subspace interventions can activate dormant pathways, so recovery alone does not prove the natural mechanism, user intent, or validation improvement. [Attribution patching](https://aclanthology.org/2024.blackboxnlp-1.25/), [interpretability illusions](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/70b8505ac79e3e131756f793cd80eb8d-Abstract-Conference.html)
